description: The requestor's view of one request: the form read-only, the stage it has reached, why it was returned or rejected if it was, and the one action available right now — edit, submit, view the PDF, or fill in the satisfaction form. It is the destination of every row click in My Requests.

docs: IRMS-old/TASKS.md (rejection notes visible to requestor, activity log UI)

happy_path.action: clicks a row in My Requests
happy_path.result: the detail page: title, document number, status chip, stepper, read-only form
the stepper shows how far it has travelled and the activity feed shows who did what, when

happy_path.action: presses Edit Request while it is a draft or returned
presses Submit Request on a draft
happy_path.result: submits in place without going through the edit page and the status chip updates

happy_path.action: presses View PDF on a submitted request
sees the CSM banner after final approval

alternate_paths.name: Returned by IDO
alternate_paths.result: the page says so in the subtitle and the reviewer's note is shown in full, above the form — the requestor must not have to open an accordion to find out why

alternate_paths.name: Rejected at any stage
alternate_paths.trigger: any of the five rejection statuses
alternate_paths.result: the rejection note from the audit log is shown the same way, and Edit and Submit are both absent

alternate_paths.name: Deferred to next year
alternate_paths.result: the status chip and an explanation that the request was valid but has no budget allocated this year

alternate_paths.name: A staff member opens it
alternate_paths.trigger: any staff role follows a link
alternate_paths.result: read-only access is allowed by getById, but no requestor action is offered — staff act from their own review pages

alternate_paths.name: Another requestor's id
alternate_paths.result: FORBIDDEN from getById; the page renders the error state, not a blank form

trpc_procedures.name: getById
guards: the caller is the owner OR holds a staff role (IDO_OFFICER, IDO_CHAIRPERSON, BUDGET_OFFICER, DIRECTOR)
trpc_procedures.description: One request with its audit logs ordered oldest-first, each joined to its actor. ADMIN is deliberately NOT a staff role here — an admin manages accounts and never reads a request.

pages.name: RequestDetailPage

page_header.title: {finalTitle ?? title}
page_header.subtitle: Status-dependent — draft, returned, under review, or approved

components.name: RequestForm
components.heroui_note: Typography per CLAUDE.md. Reused from spec 005 with forceReadOnly.
components.description: The same component the create page uses, in read-only mode. The side rail carries the status chip and whichever of Submit / Edit / View PDF applies.

components.name: RejectionNotice
components.description: Shows WHY a request was returned, rejected or deferred, using the note from the most recent negative audit log. status 'warning' for a return, 'danger' for a rejection, 'info' for a deferral. This is the IRMS-old open task 'rejection notes visible to requestor'.

components.name: RequestActivityFeed
components.heroui_note: Typography per CLAUDE.md. AppTimeline replaces the hand-built ol/rail/dot markup that IRMS-old logged as a UI defect.
components.description: One AppTimeline entry per audit log: actor is the person's name, title is the action in sentence case, summary is the status transition, detail is the note. order 'oldest-first' because this is a process, not a feed. For a requestor the feed is filtered to the actions that concern them; staff pages pass no filter and see everything.

components.name: CsmPromptBanner
components.description: Renders only when completionStatus is CSM_PENDING. 'Your request has been approved — fill out the satisfaction form to complete it', with the action navigating to the CSM page.

components.name: RequestCommentThread
components.heroui_note: None. Defined in spec 008 and mounted here.
components.description: The conversation between the requestor and whoever is processing the request.

actions.name: submitRequest
actions.description: Only while DRAFT or RETURNED — submits without re-opening the form

actions.name: viewPdf
actions.description: Once the request has been submitted. Available to every role that can read the request, not just the owner.

actions.name: openCsm
actions.description: Only while completionStatus is CSM_PENDING and the viewer owns the request

functional: The heading shows finalTitle when IDO has set one, with the requestor's original title beneath it as 'Original title: …' — the requestor must be able to see that it was changed and to what.
The document number is shown next to the status chip once issued, and nothing is shown in its place before that.
Edit and Submit appear only for DRAFT and RETURNED, and only for the owner.
View PDF appears for any submitted request and for every role allowed to read it — a reviewer following a link must be able to open the same document (an explicit IRMS-old fix).
The rejection or return note is shown above the form, in full, sourced from the newest audit log whose action is a return, rejection or deferral.

The activity feed for a requestor shows only the actions that concern them: returns, rejections and the deferral. Internal recommendations and stage approvals are staff detail and stay on the staff pages.
The CSM banner appears only while completionStatus is CSM_PENDING, and only for the owner.
Attachments are shown as a download list, never as an editable dropzone, on this page.
authorization: Route gate: assertAuthenticatedFn only — the page itself is not role-gated because five roles may legitimately read a request.
Server gate: getById allows the owner or a staff role and throws FORBIDDEN otherwise. That is the real gate; the route gate is only about being signed in.
ADMIN is not a staff role for reading requests. An admin who follows a link gets FORBIDDEN, which is correct — they manage accounts.
Every requestor action (submit, edit) re-checks ownership on the server; the buttons being hidden is not a gate.
The CSM route and its procedures check ownership independently (spec 015) — the banner being hidden is not a gate either.
ux: The subtitle names the state in the requestor's words: 'This request is a draft and has not been submitted yet', 'This request was returned by IDO — update it and resubmit', 'Under review by the Campus Director'.
Exactly one primary action is offered at a time. A draft offers Submit as primary and Edit as secondary; a submitted request offers View PDF and nothing else.
The rejection notice is a banner, not a row in the feed — the reason a request stopped must not require reading a timeline.
Loading is a skeleton of the real layout, not a spinner, because the page is tall and a spinner tells the reader nothing about what is coming.
The activity feed is oldest-first: it is a process moving forwards, not a news feed.

rules.zod_rule: path param, non-empty; a missing request yields NOT_FOUND from getById

server_guards.guard: caller is the owner OR holds IDO_OFFICER, IDO_CHAIRPERSON, BUDGET_OFFICER or DIRECTOR
ownership and an editable status — as spec 005
server_guards.error: FORBIDDEN — Access denied / Request cannot be submitted in its current status

covers: the owner can read their own request
an IDO_OFFICER can read someone else's request
a DIRECTOR can read someone else's request
another USER cannot — FORBIDDEN, not NOT_FOUND, so the id is not confirmed either way
audit logs come back oldest-first with their actor joined
picks the newest negative audit log when there are several
renders nothing when the request has never been returned or rejected
a return renders as warning and a rejection as danger
a draft shows Submit and Edit and no View PDF
a submitted request shows View PDF and neither Submit nor Edit
a returned request shows the IDO note above the form
an approved request shows the CSM banner and it navigates to the CSM page
a USER opening another user's request id sees the error state, not an empty form

acceptance_criteria.given: a DRAFT owned by the viewer
acceptance_criteria.then: Submit Request and Edit Request are both offered and View PDF is not

acceptance_criteria.given: a request returned by IDO with the note 'Attach the floor plan'
acceptance_criteria.then: that note is visible above the form without any interaction

acceptance_criteria.given: a request whose finalTitle differs from title
acceptance_criteria.then: the heading shows finalTitle and the original title is shown beneath it

acceptance_criteria.given: an APPROVED request with completionStatus CSM_PENDING
acceptance_criteria.then: the CSM banner is shown and leads to /requests/$requestId/csm

acceptance_criteria.given: a BUDGET_OFFICER following a link to a submitted request
acceptance_criteria.then: they can read it and can open the PDF, and no requestor action is offered

acceptance_criteria.given: a USER requesting another user's request id
acceptance_criteria.then: it throws FORBIDDEN and the page shows the error state

edge_cases: FORBIDDEN rather than NOT_FOUND on a request that exists but is not yours — but the two must not be distinguishable by timing or by message, or the endpoint becomes an id oracle.
The rejection notice reads the audit log, not a column on the request; a rejection recorded without a note must render the notice with the status and no body rather than an empty box.

A request can be both RETURNED (by IDO) and later resubmitted; the notice must show the note only while the request is still in the returned state, or a request under review keeps displaying an old complaint.
finalTitle may equal title, in which case the 'Original title' line is noise and must be suppressed.
The CSM banner and the CSM route both gate on ownership independently — hiding the banner for a staff viewer is not enough.
The activity filter for requestors is a whitelist. A new negative action added later and not added to the list silently disappears from the requestor's view.
out_of_scope: The comment thread's own behaviour — spec 008.
The staff review pages — specs 010-014; a staff member reading this page gets no action controls here.
